claims.text: The proposed material is a nanocrystalline refractory high-entropy alloy in the W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf system.
Sputtering can produce this alloy with a fine-grained, homogeneous microstructure.
Adding trace Hf and applying a tailored heat treatment will promote Hf segregation at grain boundaries.
The resulting grain-boundary Hf segregation will remain stable under high-temperature and irradiation exposure.
Optional co-doping can help lock in the Hf grain-boundary segregation.
The intervention will form stable Hf-enriched grain-boundary complexion layers.
Hf-enriched grain boundaries will pin dislocations and inhibit dislocation mobility.
Hf-enriched grain boundaries will act as sites for recombination of irradiation-induced defects.
The segregated complexion layers will slow irradiation-induced defect coalescence.
Co-doping, if used, will stabilize the segregated layers against irradiation-induced de-segregation.
Relative to untreated nanocrystalline W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf, the intervention will increase yield strength.
Relative to untreated nanocrystalline W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf, the intervention will increase hardness.
The intervention will reduce grain growth during high-temperature irradiation.
The intervention will diminish helium-bubble formation during high-temperature irradiation.
The expected benefits apply at approximately 900 °C under irradiation by approximately 200 keV helium ions.
Long-term Hf-segregation stability under prolonged irradiation remains uncertain.
The contribution of any additional co-dopant remains uncertain.
Performance outside the specified temperature and irradiation conditions remains uncertain.

contradictions.description: The initial and baseline materials are already identified as W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf alloys, while the intervention and experiment describe introducing trace Hf as though Hf were absent from the baseline. The intended base and modified Hf concentrations are therefore internally ambiguous.
